name: NetBox

publisher_source.quote: NetBox Labs are the commercial stewards of NetBox.

description: NetBox models and documents network infrastructure, defines its intended state and makes that data available to automation tools through APIs and a web interface.

description_source.quote: NetBox functions as the **source of truth** for your network infrastructure. Its job is to define and validate the _intended state_ of all network components and resources. NetBox does not interact with network nodes directly; rather, it makes this data available programmatically to purpose-built automation, monitoring, and assurance tools.

license_source.quote: By using NetBox—open-source, Cloud, or Enterprise—clients rely on the leading source of truth for network management and automation.

claims.quote: NetBox functions as the **source of truth** for your network infrastructure. Its job is to define and validate the _intended state_ of all network components and resources.
claims.reasoning: Storing and validating the intended state of the network is the stated main purpose of NetBox.

claims.quote: By providing a single robust user interface and programmable APIs for everything from cable maps to device configurations, NetBox serves as the central source of truth for the modern network.
claims.reasoning: NetBox provides a user interface for its own data, but not dashboards or interfaces for the rest of an automation system.

notes: The open-source code is in the netbox-community GitHub organization under the Apache 2.0 license (GitHub API reports Apache-2.0). NetBox Labs sells NetBox Cloud and NetBox Enterprise. The NetBox Labs home page (https://netboxlabs.com/) says its commercial platform adds 'Live infrastructure state compared to intent in real time'; this was not claimed for open-source NetBox because the README says 'NetBox does not interact with network nodes directly'.

name: Nautobot

publisher_source.quote: Network to Code is the sponsor and official steward of Nautobot.

description: Nautobot stores the intended state of a network in extensible data models and runs automation jobs against that data, with REST and GraphQL APIs and an app framework.

description_source.quote: Nautobot is the open source **Network Source of Truth** and **Network Automation Platform** for enterprises operating complex networks at scale.

license_source.quote: **Commercial editions** from Network to Code build on the same open source Nautobot core.

claims.quote: Nautobot's data models define the _intended state_ of your network: locations and racks, devices and interfaces, IP address space, VLANs, circuits, cables, and more.
claims.reasoning: Defining and storing the intended network state, with validation rules, is the main purpose of Nautobot.

claims.quote: Nautobot Jobs execute against your network data on demand or on a schedule, with permissions, logging, and approvals built in.
claims.reasoning: Jobs run on demand or on a schedule and webhooks connect other tools, but coordinating automation in response to events is a secondary feature, not the main purpose.

notes: The quotes come from the README shown on the GitHub repository page (raw file: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nautobot/nautobot/develop/README.md). The GitHub API reports the license as Apache-2.0. Open-source apps (Golden Configuration, Device Onboarding) may add Executor and Collector features; these were not claimed because they are separate apps.

description: dcTrack is data center infrastructure management software that records physical assets, capacity and power and network connections, and manages change requests for data center equipment.

description_source.quote: Detailed data center business intelligence and analytics about your infrastructure and visual mappings help you manage placement of your IT equipment, make informed capacity management decisions, and keep track of your data center assets.

license_source.quote: Customers on maintenance receive software support services and access to new software releases.

claims.quote: Map physical relationships between all of these devices and see how the entire power and network chain in the data center is connected down to the port level.
claims.reasoning: dcTrack stores the planned physical layer (racks, power, cabling, ports) but not logical network configuration or operational expectations.

claims.quote: 3D color-coded, floor map overlays show power, cooling, and capacity data
claims.reasoning: dcTrack provides 3D views and dashboards for its own data center data, not an interface for a whole network automation system.

notes: The site footer names 'Sunbird Software, Inc.' and '© 2026 Sunbird Inc.'. No page found that names dcTrack's publisher in one sentence, so the publisher_source quote names the product under the Sunbird brand on Sunbird's own site. The license_model 'commercial' is inferred: the sources mention quotes, maintenance contracts and trials but do not state a license. Sunbird monitoring features (Power IQ, DCIM Monitoring) are separate products and were not claimed for dcTrack.

name: phpIPAM
description: phpIPAM is a web application for IP address management that tracks IPv4 and IPv6 subnets and addresses, VLANs, VRFs and devices, with subnet scanning and a REST API.

description_source.quote: phpIPAM is a free, open source IP address management tool with IPv4/IPv6 support, VLAN management, REST API, and Docker deployment.

license_source.quote: GNU GENERAL PUBLIC LICENSE Version 3, 29 June 2007

claims.reasoning: phpIPAM stores the planned IP addressing, VLANs and VRFs, which is only one part of the desired network state.

claims.quote: Automatic subnet scanning / IP status checks
claims.reasoning: Scanning reads whether addresses are in use, which is a narrow side feature of retrieving actual network state.

notes: The GPL-3.0 text is stored in the repository at misc/gpl-3.0.txt; the GitHub API does not report a license for the repository. The phpipam.net home page states 'free, open source'. The site's news posts are written by 'MihaP'; no page found names a company behind the project.
